title: SRE Play Compiler and Incident Scenario Template Library
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This document describes the SRE Play Compiler — a lightweight, repeatable process and template library that converts SLO, error-budget, and capacity signals into executable incident plays and scenario artifacts. The Play Compiler is intended for oncall responders, runbook authors, and automation engineers who need consistent, testable, and versionable incident responses for inference services (hosted, dedicated, and private).

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-action by producing ready-to-run playbooks from a small set of telemetry inputs.
- Standardize decision points (when to throttle, when to failover, when to scale).
- Provide artifacts for tabletop exercises, automated runbook runners, and post-incident analysis.

When to use the Play Compiler:
1) When an SLO crosses warning/breach thresholds and a repeatable mitigation is applicable.
2) When onboarding a new model/service and you want pre-baked degradation plays.
3) During chaos or capacity drills to generate scenario manifests for simulation.

Key concepts and outputs:
- Scenario Manifest (YAML/JSON): machine-readable incident description (signals, thresholds, impacted tenants, recommended mitigations).
- Play Script (Confluence + CLI): human-readable step-by-step play for oncall responders with verification steps and rollback criteria.
- Automation Hooks: mapping of play steps to automation runbooks (autoscaling commands, traffic-shift jobs, model variant swap).
- Evidence Template: telemetry snapshot specification required for post-incident review.

Play Compiler workflow (high level):
1. Input signals: SLO burn rate, latency P95/P99, tail latency distribution, token backlog, queue depth, model memory pressure, cross-region health.
2. Classifier: maps signal pattern to scenario archetype (degradation, capacity-exhaustion, noisy-tenant, kernel OOM, quantized-tail-latency).
3. Template selection: pick scenario manifest from template library and parameterize using service metadata (owner, region, current capacity pool).
4. Output artifact generation: produce Scenario Manifest, Play Script, Automation Hook config, and Evidence Template.
5. Optional CI pipeline: compile and validate artifacts in a staging runner before publishing to oncall dashboard.

Template library (examples):
- noisy-tenant-throttle: recommended for per-tenant token spikes that exceed burst limits.
- prefix-cache-miss-storm: when cache miss rates exceed 30% and request CPU rises >40%.
- kv-cache-eviction-wave: when KV cache evictions correlate with latency tail.
- cross-region-failover: region N+1 health suspect with >5% error propagation.
- quantized-oom-degradation: memory pressure on quantized kernels causing OOM cascades.

Play Script structure (required sections):
1) Situation snapshot: concise summary with affected service, model, region, and primary signals.
2) Impact statement: list of customer-visible symptoms and preliminary severity.
3) Owner and contacts: primary oncall, service owner, SRE escalation contact, pager channel.
4) Immediate mitigations (ordered by speed-to-effect): short, tested commands and the expected verification metric.
5) Medium-term mitigations: capacity adjustments, traffic routing, model variant swaps.
6) Recovery and rollback criteria: exact thresholds and verification windows.
7) Post-incident evidence checklist: telemetry slices and artifacts to archive.

Example Immediate Mitigations table (CSV-style):
| Mitigation | Command | Expected effect | Verification metric | Max safe duration | Owner |
| throttle-noisy-tenant | rwdctl tenant throttle --tenant-id {TENANT} --rate 50rps | reduce token burn | tenant token/sec falls 60% in 60s | 30m | oncall |
| spin-up-warm-pool | rwdctl pool scale --pool inference-warm --delta 4 --priority low-latency | increase concurrency headroom | cluster free-gpu > 4 | 20m | infra |
| variant-fallback | rwdctl model swap --service {SVC} --from {MODEL-A} --to {MODEL-A-quant} | fallback to compatible quantized model | p95 latency decreases by 30% | 60m | model-owner |

Automation Hook mapping (examples):
- throttle-noisy-tenant -> autoscaler webhook (namespace: rwd/autoscale)
- spin-up-warm-pool -> infra-runbook job (k8s job: rwd-warm-pool-scale)
- variant-fallback -> canary-deployer endpoint (POST /deployments/canary-swap)

Scenario Manifest example (JSON snippet for automation pipelines):
{
  "scenario_id": "noisy-tenant-2026-02-10-az1",
  "service": "inference-api",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "signals": ["tenant_token_rate>1000", "token_backlog>5000"],
  "recommended_mitigations": ["throttle-noisy-tenant", "spin-up-warm-pool"],
  "evidence_spec": ["tenancy:token-rate-1m", "node:gpu-memory-1m"]
}

(When stored in the Play Compiler repository this JSON is validated against the scenario schema. The Play Compiler emits a version tag and CI result.)

Runbook: Step-by-step (play generated for noisy-tenant-throttle):
1. Confirm alert and check situation snapshot: gather p95/p99, tenant token/sec, queue depth. (CLI: rwdctl alerts get --alert-id {ALERT})
2. Post a short status update to #oncall-status with summary.
3. Execute throttle: rwdctl tenant throttle --tenant-id {TENANT} --rate 50rps. Record command output in incident evidence.
4. Verify tenant token/sec over next 60s and p95 latency for that tenant. If metrics move as expected, continue to medium-term mitigations.
5. If no improvement in 60s, escalate to infra and spin-up-warm-pool: rwdctl pool scale --pool inference-warm --delta 4.
6. If spin-up fails or memory pressure increases, perform variant-fallback.
7. When service stabilizes for 30 minutes within thresholds, begin rollback of temporary throttles and scale actions.
8. Archive evidence: attach scenario manifest, command logs, tracer snapshots, and query exports to the post-incident ticket.

Validation and testing guidance:
- Unit test scenario manifests with the Play Compiler test harness (rwd-play-compiler test --manifest ./scenarios/noisy-tenant.json).
- Run tabletop with synthetic telemetry (rwd-play-compiler simulate --manifest ./scenarios/noisy-tenant.json --duration 10m).
- CI gating: every change to a template must include a simulation run that demonstrates mitigation reduces p95 by configured percent within the time window.

SLO and error budget integration:
- Each generated play must include explicit error-budget impact estimates (tokens lost, % SLO burn avoided). Example: estimated SLO burn reduction: 0.12% over 1h.
- Use SLO thresholds to select mitigation aggressiveness (warning vs breach). Warning plays aim for surgical mitigations (throttles, tenant-level controls). Breach plays may include heavier actions (region failover, global capacity reallocation).

Capacity planning tie-ins:
- Templates are annotated with headroom requirements (GPU count, warm-pool size, cold-start time).
- Play Compiler can generate capacity-run requests for infra when repeated plays imply sustained headroom shortfall. Example: after 3 noisy-tenant plays in 24h, create capacity request: {"reason":"recurrent noisy tenant", "delta_gpus":8, "priority":"high"}.

Post-incident evidence template (minimum required artifacts):
- scenario manifest (compiler output)
- 5m/1m/30s metric slices for p50/p95/p99, request throughput, queue depth, tenant token/sec
- tracer capture (start/end timestamps) for three representative requests
- rwdctl command logs and automation-run logs
- model and runtime kernel versions

Operational governance and ownership:
- Template authorship: every template must include an owner and a secondary reviewer. Owners are responsible for annual validation.
- Play lifecycle: draft -> in_review -> published. Changes to published templates require CI simulation passing and sign-off by reviewer.
- Evidence retention: artifacts from any Play Compiler run are archived to the SRE evidence bucket for 90 days by default, 1 year for incidents marked Sev2 or higher.

Appendix A: Common signal-to-archetype mapping (quick reference):
- tenant_token_rate spike + queue depth rising -> noisy-tenant-throttle
- p99 increases with stable throughput -> prefix-cache-miss-storm
- node oom events + eviction spikes -> kv-cache-eviction-wave
- region 502/5xx uptick + TCP resets -> cross-region-failover

Appendix B: Example CI command matrix (for template PRs):
1) rwd-play-compiler lint ./scenarios/*.json
2) rwd-play-compiler test --manifest ./scenarios/noisy-tenant.json --retries 2
3) rwd-play-compiler simulate --manifest ./scenarios/noisy-tenant.json --duration 5m --assert p95_drop>=25

Contact and ownership:
- Play Compiler owner: Aisha Patel (SRE Tools)
- Reviewer rotation: quarterly — contact eng-sre leads to join the rotation.

Glossary:
- Play Compiler: tool/process that generates incident plays from telemetry.
- Scenario Manifest: structured incident representation for automation and CI.
- Evidence Template: minimal artifact list required for post-incident review.

Related pages and next steps:
- Add new template: follow the Template Authoring Guide and include unit tests and simulation artifacts.
- To request an integration with automation runners, open an infra change with tag "play-compiler-integration".

This document is intended to be living. Template authors should schedule a validation run at least once per quarter and update manifests when service topology or autoscaling knobs change.
